newsitem.title: INDIA: UK's Major urges India to open up insurance.
newsitem.headline: UK's Major urges India to open up insurance.

text.p: British Prime Minister John Major urged India on Thursday to open up its insurance sector to foreign competition, cut tariffs on imports of consumer goods and offer protection to intellectual property.

Major told the Confederation of Indian Industry's annual meeting in Calcutta that three key sectors for further economic progress in India were telecommunications, financial services and consumer goods.
"Opening up the insurance sector, for example, would also contribute significantly to long-term growth, providing scarce funds for infrastructural development," Major said.
The Indian government has promised to open up its state-controlled insurance sector to private firms, both domestic and foreign.
"Opening up trade in consumer goods would create further investment and growth more widely," he said.

"Indian tariffs are still high by international standards, especially when countervailing duty is added," he said. "I hope that early progress can be made in bringing them down too, as well as in removing import controls and in improving the protection of intellectual property."
